lines.text: A ladder leans over a big box and reaches a wall.
lines.caption: A ladder leans over a big box and reaches a wall.

lines.text: Most kids stop halfway and pick the wrong answer. <short pause> Not us!
lines.caption: Most kids stop halfway and pick the wrong answer. Not us!

lines.text: Hello, my name is Vantee! Let's climb this one together.
lines.caption: Hello, my name is Vantee! Let's climb this one together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A box twelve feet tall and twelve feet deep sits on the ground, against a wall.
lines.caption: A box twelve feet tall and twelve feet deep sits on the ground, against a wall.

lines.text: A ladder has its foot on the ground, nine feet from the box.
lines.caption: A ladder has its foot on the ground, nine feet from the box.

lines.text: It touches the top outer edge of the box, and reaches the wall.
lines.caption: It touches the top outer edge of the box, and reaches the wall.

lines.text: How long is the ladder, in feet?
lines.caption: How long is the ladder, in feet?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we really know?
lines.caption: So what do we really know?

lines.text: The foot is nine feet from the box. The box is twelve deep, so the wall is twenty-one feet away.
lines.caption: The foot is nine feet from the box. The box is twelve deep, so the wall is twenty-one feet away.

lines.text: The ladder just touches the box's top corner, twelve feet up.
lines.caption: The ladder just touches the box's top corner, twelve feet up.

lines.text: We need the WHOLE ladder, from the ground all the way to the wall.
lines.caption: We need the WHOLE ladder, from the ground all the way to the wall.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's look at the small triangle, from the foot to the box's corner.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's look at the small triangle, from the foot to the box's corner.

lines.text: Going nine feet across, the ladder rises twelve feet.
lines.caption: Going nine feet across, the ladder rises twelve feet.

lines.text: A straight ladder keeps the same steepness the whole way up.
lines.caption: A straight ladder keeps the same steepness the whole way up.

lines.text: Twelve up for nine across is the same as four up for every three across.
lines.caption: Twelve up for nine across is the same as four up for every three across.

lines.text: The wall is twenty-one feet away. That's seven groups of three.
lines.caption: The wall is twenty-one feet away. That's seven groups of three.

lines.text: So the ladder rises seven groups of four. Seven times four is twenty-eight.
lines.caption: So the ladder rises seven groups of four. Seven times four is twenty-eight.

lines.text: The ladder meets the wall twenty-eight feet up!
lines.caption: The ladder meets the wall twenty-eight feet up!

lines.text: Now we have a big right triangle. Twenty-one across, twenty-eight up.
lines.caption: Now we have a big right triangle. Twenty-one across, twenty-eight up.

lines.text: The ladder is the long side. Let's use Pythagoras.
lines.caption: The ladder is the long side. Let's use Pythagoras.

lines.text: Twenty-one squared is four hundred forty-one. Twenty-eight squared is seven hundred eighty-four.
lines.caption: Twenty-one squared is four hundred forty-one. Twenty-eight squared is seven hundred eighty-four.

lines.text: Add them up. That's one thousand two hundred twenty-five.
lines.caption: Add them up. That's one thousand two hundred twenty-five.

lines.text: And thirty-five times thirty-five is one thousand two hundred twenty-five.
lines.caption: And thirty-five times thirty-five is one thousand two hundred twenty-five.

lines.text: So the ladder is thirty-five feet long. The answer is D!
lines.caption: So the ladder is thirty-five feet long. The answer is D!

lines.text: Here is another way. The box corner cuts the ladder into two pieces.
lines.caption: Here is another way. The box corner cuts the ladder into two pieces.

lines.text: The lower piece: nine across, twelve up. That's the three, four, five triangle, times three.
lines.caption: The lower piece: nine across, twelve up. That's the three, four, five triangle, times three.

lines.text: So the lower piece is fifteen feet.
lines.caption: So the lower piece is fifteen feet.

lines.text: The upper piece runs over the box, twelve feet across.
lines.caption: The upper piece runs over the box, twelve feet across.

lines.text: Same steepness, so it rises four for every three. Twelve across means sixteen up.
lines.caption: Same steepness, so it rises four for every three. Twelve across means sixteen up.

lines.text: Sides twelve, sixteen and twenty. That's the three, four, five triangle, times four.
lines.caption: Sides twelve, sixteen and twenty. That's the three, four, five triangle, times four.

lines.text: So the upper piece is twenty feet. Fifteen plus twenty is thirty-five! It matches.
lines.caption: So the upper piece is twenty feet. Fifteen plus twenty is thirty-five! It matches.

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the pieces are nice triangles, the numbers stay small.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the pieces are nice triangles, the numbers stay small.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Fifteen is just the lower piece. It stops at the box's corner.
lines.caption: Fifteen is just the lower piece. It stops at the box's corner.

lines.text: Twenty is what you'd get if you only measured the upper piece, from the box to the wall.
lines.caption: Twenty is what you'd get if you only measured the upper piece, from the box to the wall.

lines.text: Twenty-eight is how high the ladder reaches on the wall. That's a height, not the ladder's length.
lines.caption: Twenty-eight is how high the ladder reaches on the wall. That's a height, not the ladder's length.

lines.text: Thirty-seven is what you'd get if you added nine across and twenty-eight up.
lines.caption: Thirty-seven is what you'd get if you added nine across and twenty-eight up.

lines.text: But you can't just add across and up. The ladder cuts the corner, so use Pythagoras.
lines.caption: But you can't just add across and up. The ladder cuts the corner, so use Pythagoras.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Read the question again: the ladder goes all the way to the wall.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Read the question again: the ladder goes all the way to the wall.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Let's try a new ladder, one with different numbers.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Let's try a new ladder, one with different numbers.

lines.text: This box is eight feet tall and nine feet deep, against a wall.
lines.caption: This box is eight feet tall and nine feet deep, against a wall.

lines.text: The ladder's foot is six feet from the box. It touches the top outer edge and reaches the wall.
lines.caption: The ladder's foot is six feet from the box. It touches the top outer edge and reaches the wall.

lines.text: How long is this ladder?
lines.caption: How long is this ladder?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Six across, eight up. That's four up for every three across again.
lines.caption: Let's check. Six across, eight up. That's four up for every three across again.

lines.text: The wall is six plus nine, which is fifteen feet away. That's five groups of three.
lines.caption: The wall is six plus nine, which is fifteen feet away. That's five groups of three.

lines.text: So the ladder rises five groups of four. That's twenty feet up the wall.
lines.caption: So the ladder rises five groups of four. That's twenty feet up the wall.

lines.text: Fifteen across, twenty up. Fifteen squared plus twenty squared is six hundred twenty-five.
lines.caption: Fifteen across, twenty up. Fifteen squared plus twenty squared is six hundred twenty-five.

lines.text: Twenty-five times twenty-five is six hundred twenty-five. So the ladder is twenty-five feet!
lines.caption: Twenty-five times twenty-five is six hundred twenty-five. So the ladder is twenty-five feet!

lines.text: Check with pieces: ten below the corner, fifteen above. Ten plus fifteen is twenty-five!
lines.caption: Check with pieces: ten below the corner, fifteen above. Ten plus fifteen is twenty-five!

lines.text: If you found twenty-five, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found twenty-five, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: A straight line rises the same amount for every step across.
lines.caption: A straight line rises the same amount for every step across.

lines.text: So use the small triangle to find how high it goes, then use Pythagoras for the length.
lines.caption: So use the small triangle to find how high it goes, then use Pythagoras for the length.

lines.text: Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time. Vantee, signing off!
lines.caption: Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time. Vantee, signing off!
